verdict.rationale: RustDesk's docs say it supports H264/H265 hardware codecs, which covers the hardware-encoding half of the story. The vendor makes no first-party latency claim. Hands-on reports are mixed: heavy daily users find it smoother than AnyDesk, even for YouTube playback, but others found it extremely laggy or slow via the default relay. missing for 10: documented low-latency or interactive-performance claims, consistent independent latency evidence, details on how and when hardware encoding is enabled per platform.

support.subject: As a power user, the stream is hardware-encoded and low-latency enough for interactive work, not just passive viewing

citations.quote: Supports VP8 / VP9 / AV1 software codecs, and H264 / H265 hardware codecs.
Uses RustDesk 12 hours a day, 6 days a week, on multiple computers; visually much better than AnyDesk. YouTube plays fine where AnyDesk chugs
